title: Romania's Money Game That Paid 8x… Until It Didn't 🇷🇴💸
yt_title: Romania's Money Game That Paid 8x… Until It Didn't 🇷🇴💸
yt_description:
In 1992, a former accountant named Ioan Stoica launched Caritas in Brașov, Romania, then moved it to Cluj. The promise: bring your money and get back eight times as much within a few months. Early players really were paid, a local newspaper printed long lists of winners, and the mayor of Cluj publicly backed the game. Estimates of the number of players range from 2 to 8 million, in a country of about 23 million. But the winners were paid with newcomers' money. In 1994 Caritas collapsed, owing about $450 million. Stoica ended up serving less than two years.
The lesson: a list of winners tells you nothing about the people still waiting behind them.

script: In 1992, a former accountant in Romania made an incredible offer. Bring him your money. In a few months, get back eight times as much. He called it Caritas. Latin for charity. Officially, a mutual-aid game. It started in Brașov, then moved to the city of Cluj. And here is the strange part. It paid. The first players really got eight times their money. A local newspaper printed long lists of the lucky winners. Page after page of names. The mayor of Cluj appeared with him in public and defended the game. People emptied their savings. Queues wrapped around the block. Estimates say between two and eight million Romanians played. In a country of twenty-three million. But there was no business behind it. The winners were paid with the newcomers' money. When new money slowed, the payouts stopped. In 1994, Caritas collapsed, owing about four hundred and fifty million dollars. The founder went to prison for less than two years. Most players never saw their money again. This is the winners' list trap. Psychologists call it social proof, mixed with survivorship bias. We see the people who won. We never see the long line still waiting behind them. So when a deal shows you a list of winners, ask: who is paying them? And where is the list of everyone who lost?
